skill.name: auth-wechat-miniprogram
skill.description: Guide agents to implement native WeChat Mini Program authentication with CloudBase, including wx.cloud setup and verified caller identity.
skill.summary: Implement native CloudBase authentication for WeChat Mini Programs using wx.cloud, OPENID, UNIONID, and cloud functions.
skill.author: tencentcloudbase

security_audit.summary: Static detections are false positives caused by Markdown inline code, fenced JavaScript examples, reference URLs, and sibling skill paths. The review found two medium-risk content issues: an authorization example that relies on client-supplied owner data and examples that log sensitive identifiers.

remediation.issue: Authorization example uses client-supplied owner data.
remediation.suggestion: Revise the example to fetch the resource owner from server-side storage and compare that value to verified OPENID.

remediation.issue: Examples log OPENID, UNIONID, and auth user objects.
remediation.suggestion: Mask identifiers in examples and state that full identity logs should be limited to local debugging.

semantic_findings.title: Client-Supplied Authorization Boundary
semantic_findings.description: The authorization example compares verified OPENID to event.resourceOwnerId. In a Mini Program cloud function, event data is client-supplied, so this can teach unsafe ownership checks if used alone.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code example directly uses event.resourceOwnerId as the authorization boundary. Legitimate use is possible, but auth guidance should derive ownership from server-side data.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Identifier Logging in Examples

content.user_title: Build WeChat Mini Program Auth with CloudBase
content.value_statement: WeChat Mini Program auth is easy to misapply when CloudBase identity is automatic. This skill gives practical patterns for wx.cloud, OPENID, UNIONID, and cloud functions.
actual_capabilities: Explains automatic CloudBase identity injection for WeChat Mini Program cloud function calls.
Shows how to initialize wx.cloud in a Mini Program entry point.
Provides cloud function examples using wx-server-sdk and cloud.getWXContext().
Covers OPENID, APPID, and optional UNIONID handling.
Distinguishes native Mini Program auth from Web-based WeChat login.
Describes v3 Web SDK methods for OpenID and phone authorization flows.
limitations: Does not cover Web-based WeChat login pages or OAuth flows.
Does not configure CloudBase providers, console settings, or environment linking.
Examples require review before production use, especially authorization checks and logging.
Assumes the project already uses CloudBase and WeChat Mini Program APIs.

use_cases.title: Implement Mini Program Identity
use_cases.description: Add native CloudBase identity handling to a WeChat Mini Program without building a separate login page.

use_cases.title: Review Cloud Function Auth
use_cases.description: Check how a cloud function reads OPENID, APPID, and UNIONID before using user-specific data.

use_cases.title: Choose Native or Web Auth
use_cases.description: Decide whether a feature should use native Mini Program identity or a separate Web authentication flow.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize CloudBase Auth
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add native WeChat Mini Program auth to my CloudBase app. Ask me for missing env details first.

prompt_templates.title: Read Caller Identity
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a cloud function pattern that reads OPENID, APPID, and UNIONID with wx-server-sdk. Include error handling guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Design User Data Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design user-specific database access for a Mini Program. Use OPENID safely and avoid exposing identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Existing Auth Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Mini Program CloudBase auth flow for native login assumptions, unsafe authorization checks, and production logging risks.

output_examples.input: User asks how to identify the caller in a CloudBase cloud function.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains CloudBase caller context, when UNIONID appears, and how to return only required identity fields.

output_examples.input: User needs Mini Program auth setup for a new CloudBase app.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for the environment ID, confirms CloudBase binding, and outlines initialization during app launch.

output_examples.input: User wants to protect user-owned records in a Mini Program.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends server-side ownership checks with OPENID and warns against trusting client-supplied owner fields.

best_practices: Confirm the CloudBase environment ID and Mini Program binding before writing code.
Use verified OPENID from CloudBase context for user ownership decisions.
Treat logs containing OPENID, UNIONID, or phone auth data as sensitive.
anti_patterns: Do not build a Web-style login page for native Mini Program authentication.
Do not send user credentials manually when wx.cloud already passes caller identity.
Do not trust client-supplied owner identifiers as the only authorization check.

faq.question: Does this replace WeChat OAuth?
faq.answer: For native Mini Programs, CloudBase uses automatic WeChat identity. Web OAuth is a separate flow and is not covered here.

faq.question: Can this skill configure CloudBase settings?
faq.answer: No. It guides code patterns after the Mini Program is linked to a CloudBase environment.

faq.question: Is OPENID always available?
faq.answer: OPENID is available in standard Mini Program cloud function calls when CloudBase is initialized correctly.

faq.question: When should I use UNIONID?
faq.answer: Use UNIONID when the Mini Program is bound to a WeChat Open Platform account and cross-app identity is needed.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Are the examples production ready?
faq.answer: No. Review authorization logic, logging, error handling, and privacy rules before production use.
